content.comment_body: If you have a newly purchased [article_no], there was an unannounced firmware update around the end of 2016. With [product_name] software, you need to update to [version_no]. You can do this quickly via the Update Center found in the menu bar. Make sure to open the program with administrator rights, otherwise it won't function properly. After [version_no] is installed and running, check the firmware version of your [article_no]: - Diagnostics - Software - Firmware version. If it’s [version_no], select the PLC type at the bottom right of the screen as "[product_name]". If it’s [version_no], choose "[article_no].Standard". The previous version of the software ([version_no]) can still program the [version_no] variant of [article_no] hardware.

The confusion comes from mixing up the firmware versions and their names. [article_no].Standard ([version_no] to [version_no]) uses firmware [version_no] to [version_no] and works with [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. The newer hardware ([product_name]) requires firmware [version_no] and is compatible only with [product_name] [version_no].
Thanks for the clarification. Has [company_name] published any official documentation about this update?
Not directly in this format. Users have to refer to product notifications and related messages to figure it out.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to another thread titled Problems with the commands, and editing blocks from the screen. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are experiencing confusion about firmware updates and compatibility due to unclear documentation for [article_no] hardware and corresponding [product_name] software versions. The lack of direct guidance leads to mistakes in setup and programming workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect comprehensive, straightforward instructions about firmware and software compatibility for their hardware. They want clear information from [company_name] on configuring and programming new modules with [product_name].
